## Goal
`check_home` (`doctor.py:70-86`) tells a person whose data folder is missing or read-only to run `mkdir -p` or `chown -R $USER`, which do not exist on Windows (where Pat lives), and it never warns when the folder is inside a cloud-synced folder (OneDrive, Dropbox, iCloud Drive, Google Drive), which would upload the encrypted store and may lock files while the app runs. Make the fix text depend on `sys.platform` (on Windows: "Create the folder in File Explorer, or set the FREEMYID_HOME setting to a folder you can write to."), and add a `warn` (not a failure) when any path component of the data folder is named like a sync folder (case-insensitive: `onedrive`, `dropbox`, `icloud`, `google drive`, `googledrive`, `box sync`, `nextcloud`), with the plain advice to move the folder. A folder that exists and is writable is otherwise unchanged. On Windows `os.access` is unreliable for writability, so write and delete a tiny temp file in the folder instead (guarded, never raising).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. Missing folder: on `sys.platform == "linux"` the fix still mentions `mkdir -p`; on `"win32"` it mentions neither `mkdir -p` nor `chown` nor `$USER`, and says File Explorer (monkeypatch `sys.platform` and `paths.home`).
2. A folder whose path has a component `OneDrive` (any case) returns `warn` with advice to move the data folder; one named `OneDrive-notes` is not matched (whole-component match only); a normal folder is `ok`.
3. On win32 the writability probe creates and removes one file inside `tmp_path`; a read-only folder (simulate by monkeypatching the probe's `open` to raise `PermissionError`) returns `fail` with the Windows fix text.
4. The probe leaves no file behind on success or failure.
5. The unix mode check (`chmod 700` advice) is unchanged on non-Windows.
6. `check_home` never raises; ids, order and `doctor/1` keys are unchanged; existing doctor tests (including WO-283's) pass unchanged.

This is Codex code-lane work (owner, 2026-11-09): fix and improve the listed module(s) directly, with tests; don't xfail a bug you can fix here. No contract changes: public function signatures, `src/freemyid/models.py`, `interfaces.py`, schema files, `--json` shapes and documented CLI output stay as they are (additive helpers inside the listed files are fine). If the work turns out to need a contract change, stop and say so in VENDOR_STATUS.md "Questions for the owner". Fake data only, offline (fake fetchers, no network), Windows-safe paths in tests (`tmp_path`, `pathlib`, no `/tmp`). Typed, ruff-clean, small diff. Line numbers are from main at the time of writing (2026-11-09); re-check them.
